items.title: Milt Fillius interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 18, 2000
items.q: We had a librarian named Pilkington who wrote a book when he left about the college

ctx.x: What was the reason for that?

I don’t know. We had a librarian named Pilkington who wrote a book when he left about the college, and it was said that the class of 1944 was terrible and never should have been admitted. And I think his reason was maybe the same reason — that was the first class that did not require a basic background of study of Latin or Greek. It was the first time that we could get in with a romance language. I got in for example with French or German, one of the two. And Latin and Greek had been the requirement ever since.…
Those years were called the “crazy mixed up years?”
